That finding is absent from the already-consumed immutable aggregate, and the live aggregate verifier cannot run again because receipt replay is rejected. Existing smoke covers pre-consumption sealing and live tamper before consumption, but not the consume-to-phase-write race or post-consumption reviewer finding. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:232-247 and packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:455-489 — critical wave-boundary evidence loss distinct from F-029/F-030. review_inventory_wave_advance serializes and persists a completed wave, but the OPEN epoch remains writable afterward. assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence deliberately accepts a non-latest current-round fresh ReviewRun (review-run.ts:1215-1222), so a run started before the checkpoint may submit a verified finding after wave_advance releases the lock. The next evaluation sets waveStart to the prior completedAt and filters candidates by run.startedAt >= waveStart; that old run and its late finding are therefore excluded from the new wave, while the already persisted prior wave cannot be amended. A later zero-new wave can finalize and consume a receipt whose immutable family set omits this signed verified finding. The normal REVIEW gate may still surface an open critical finding, but REVIEW-to-remediation-DEV consumes only reviewInventoryRemediationGate and can proceed with the incomplete aggregate (machine.ts:732-750). Seal completed-wave run IDs, classify evidence by evidence.createdAt with explicit cutoff semantics, or reject terminals for runs started before the current wave; add a real wave_advance-then-old-run-finding negative smoke.

findings.desc: Temporal boundaries are not total-ordered, so F031/F032 can still be bypassed within one millisecond. review inventory classifies a run as current-wave when run.startedAt >= wave.completedAt/begunAt and seals it only when run.startedAt < boundary; cancel/invalidate uses the same strict-less-than test. Because all timestamps are millisecond ISO strings, a ReviewRun that actually started before wave_advance/cancel/begin but shares the exact timestamp is accepted as fresh evidence for the next wave. The handler smoke acknowledges this gap by busy-waiting until Date.now() is strictly greater than completedAt/updatedAt/finding.createdAt before exercising wave 2 and rebegin. Thus real execution has no mechanical happens-before identity: an old terminal can satisfy a supposedly independent zero-new wave, and a pre-begin finding whose ReviewRun shares begunAt can be omitted from baselineFindingIds. Replace timestamp-only admission with a signed monotonic boundary (sequence/event identity) or otherwise make equality conservatively old, while preserving an unambiguous way for genuinely post-boundary runs to prove freshness; add deterministic equal-timestamp tests without busy-waits.

packages/main/src/core/review-inventory-epoch.ts:267-274 — critical same-wave multi-run omission remains after F029-F032 remediation. For each required lane, evaluateReviewInventoryWave sorts current-wave runs newest-first and selects only the first run with any terminal; rawFindings receives findings only from that one selected run. Yet assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence explicitly permits a material-fresh non-latest run to write finding/pass evidence (review-run.ts:1215-1222). Therefore two concurrent same-lane runs can order as: older run records a verified finding, newer run records a pass; evaluation selects the newer pass and silently omits the older signed open finding from critic dispositions and the receipt. This is distinct from F031 because both runs start after the same wave boundary. The ordinary REVIEW verdict treats the older open finding as stale-run evidence rather than erased, but REVIEW-to-remediation-DEV consumes the inventory receipt without evaluateReviewVerdict (machine.ts:732-750), so an incomplete aggregate can authorize DEV. Aggregate verified findings from every eligible current-wave run while selecting one terminal only for lane coverage, or reject/supersede terminal writes with an explicit safe rule; add a real two-runs-one-lane finding-then-pass negative smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts:581-589 ProcessTreeLifecycle.terminateAndVerify: the post-SIGKILL while(true) polling loop only breaks on `!live.length` (line 583). `exceededBudget` is set at line 587 once `performance.now() >= deadline`, but that flag is never checked to exit the loop -- it is only read afterward at line 591, which is unreachable while the loop keeps spinning. A genuinely unkillable process (e.g. Linux D-state / uninterruptible I/O, which SIGKILL cannot terminate) makes `liveTargetIds()` return non-empty forever, so the loop retries every retryIntervalMs (20ms default) indefinitely and terminateAndVerify() never resolves or rejects -- the documented bounded cleanup budget (test-runner-consolidation-plan.md: process tree termination verified before publishing a terminal result) is not actually enforced for this case; the whole runner (and callers like npm test) hangs instead of fail-closing with the AggregateError budget message. No fixture in full-suite-runner-smoke.ts exercises this true-infinite/never-dies case (grep for exceededBudget/deadline/while(true)/unkillable/infinite in the smoke file returns nothing); only PID-reuse and detached-descendant-cleanup scenarios are covered.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed real and fixed. The post-SIGKILL retry loop in ProcessTreeLifecycle.terminateAndVerify broke only on !live.length; it set exceededBudget when the deadline passed but never exited, so a PID that can never be reaped (Linux D-state / uninterruptible sleep) made the loop spin forever and the documented bounded-budget AggregateError below it was unreachable. Fix keeps the fail-closed contract rather than weakening it: on deadline expiry the loop now records a lifecycle error naming the surviving PIDs (captured PID(s) still live after SIGKILL within cleanup budget: <ids>) and breaks, so control reaches the existing AggregateError throw and the terminal result is still NEGATIVE. It never publishes a clean tree while a captured child may remain, preserving the never publish a terminal result with an unknown child guarantee. Added the missing true-infinite fixture the finding called out: test:unkillable-survivor stubs only probe to return true forever (unlike the existing persistent-survivor, which dies after 30 polls), asserting the run terminates well under 30s instead of hanging and that the reason names both the exceeded 50ms cleanup budget and still live after SIGKILL. It is written standalone rather than through lifecycleFixture because that helper asserts the descendant died, which cannot hold when the probe never reports death; only probe is stubbed so the real descendant is still genuinely signalled, and the fixture reaps it explicitly afterwards. Verified: npm run test:full-suite-runner-smoke PASS (185 assertions), up from 183; npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main exits 0. Mutation check proving the new test bites: reverting the compiled dist to the unbounded form (deleting the record+break) makes the suite HANG with no output past a 90s timeout, exactly the runaway the finding predicted; the dist was then byte-restored and re-ran PASS (185).

The unconditional throw is gone. proofstory.ts now carries a comment at that site explaining why refusing the NEGATIVE verdict is what made the deadlock inescapable, and the basis requirement lives on the pass branch only, at line 582: if (args.verdict === 'pass' && !state.basisVerification.ok) throw. findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/reviewer-list.ts:168-176 (F-091 fix): computeActiveReviewers now replays every historical reviewer_forced event from story.events, correctly making a --forceReviewer mount durable across DEV round-trips and fresh review-inventory epochs (verified: RI-029/RI-030 froze requiredLanes without behavior, RI-031+ include it; mutation-check style byte-diff not needed since this is a design-gap finding, not a correctness bug). However this same fix removes the ONLY escape hatch that previously existed by accident: because forced was ephemeral before this fix (only reviewer-list.ts:254 threaded it), a mistaken or stale force silently expired on the next reviewer_list-independent call. Now that the force is durably read back from story.events with no expiry, no round/phase scoping, and no filtering by relevance, there is no unforceReviewer/remove-force command anywhere in the codebase (grep across packages/main/src and packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts for unforce/remove.*[Rr]eviewer/reviewer_unforced returns zero hits) and no documented way to reverse an operator mistake. findings.resolvedReason: Accepted and covered by a regression test, with one correction to the finding premise that I verified empirically rather than assuming. Added to packages/main/src/tasks/review-assurance-floor-smoke.ts a test driving computeActiveReviewers with a story whose events mix: an ensureCurrentReviewRound-shaped reviewer_forced event with NO reviewer field, a genuine operator reviewer_forced event for behavior, a non-reviewer_forced event that DOES carry a reviewer field, and a reviewer_forced event whose reviewer is a non-string. It asserts the real operator force mounts durably and is marked forced:true, that the non-reviewer_forced event does not mount a lane, that replay does not duplicate a lane, and that no empty lane name is ever admitted. CORRECTION to the finding as written and to my own initial restatement of it: the non-empty reviewer check is NOT the sole disambiguation. I mutation-tested it and removing .filter(name => name.length > 0) alone changed nothing observable, because the mount loop independently guards with if (!name) continue. Current final state at review-inventory.ts:85-118 (captureReviewInventoryScope): candidateSpecSetDigest = reviewInventoryDigest({schemaVersion, mode, candidates: candidates.map(row=>({path,contentHash})), queryFiltering, scanEscalationReason}) -- deliberately dropping validCandidate.artifactDigest (which bakes in headHash/materialHash verbatim, per candidate-spec-routing.ts:757-761/764-800) AND dropping storyInputDigest entirely. The commit message (git show 4f19f74f27) documents why storyInputDigest was also removed after the F-103 fix, not just narrowed: storyInputDigest is digestCandidateRoutingValue(input) over a routing input that includes changedPaths (git diff --name-only main...HEAD), and changedPaths also seeds keyword weights that flow into candidates[].score/.reasons -- two independent freshness-leak channels, not one. So the barrier now binds WHICH specs were selected and WHAT they contain (path+contentHash per candidate) plus the routing policy knobs (schemaVersion/mode/queryFiltering/scanEscalationReason), never storyInputDigest and never score/reasons. artifactDigest itself is unchanged and verifyCandidateSpecSet (candidate-spec-routing.ts:764-800) still verifies the full identity digest including headHash/materialHash, so real tampering with the candidate set is still caught; only what the OPEN-epoch barrier (persistInvalidationIfDrifted candidateChanged) compares was narrowed. This mirrors the same semantic-content-not-bookkeeping rule already documented for verificationEvidence at lines 183-191 (bound by what a verifier OBSERVED, deliberately not by freshness pins headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash/timestamp/receipt.executedAt), but the candidate-routing paragraph was never updated to state the analogous rule for the candidate set, so a reader of lines 199-203 today would reasonably expect ANY candidate_spec_route re-run to invalidate the epoch whenever HEAD or the changed-file set moves, which is no longer true. Recommended replacement text, to insert immediately after the existing sentence ending '...ProofStory contract below.' and before the current 'The epoch also signs...' sentence (lines 192-199): 'The same semantic-content-not-bookkeeping rule applies to the candidate set. The epoch signs candidateSpecSetDigest as a routing-universe projection of the current valid CandidateSpecSetArtifact -- schemaVersion, mode, each selected candidate reduced to its path and content hash, queryFiltering, and scanEscalationReason -- and corpusDigest, deliberately NOT the artifact's own artifactDigest (which bakes in headHash/materialHash verbatim as the artifact's tamper-detection identity; verifyCandidateSpecSet still verifies that full identity digest, so genuine tampering with the candidate set is still caught) and deliberately NOT storyInputDigest or any candidate's score/reasons, both of which are seeded by the changed-file set from git diff and therefore leak freshness rather than routing-universe identity. findings.desc: review-inventory.ts:109-118 captureReviewInventoryScope binds candidateSpecSetDigest to the candidate artifact's queryFiltering field verbatim (schemaVersion,mode,candidates-projected,queryFiltering,scanEscalationReason). This is a fifth, still-open freshness leak of the F-099/F-103/F-104 defect class: queryFiltering.filteredTerms is NOT a corpus-only invariant. candidate-spec-routing.ts:528 unfilteredQueryTerms = orderedQueryTerms(args.seeds.seeds, proposals); args.seeds.seeds is buildKeywordSeeds output, which at candidate-spec-routing.ts:334 seeds a term for every entry in input.changedPaths (weight 50); changedPaths is git diff --name-only main...HEAD (handlers/candidate-spec-routing.ts:141,252,294, live in production). filteredTerms (candidate-spec-routing.ts:546-553) is queryTerms.filter(overbroad-or-zero-hits) computed from documentCounts keyed by these same query terms. Concretely: an unrelated commit during the OPEN epoch that changes the diff file set (touches e.g. scripts/some-unrelated-script.mjs) shifts changedPaths, adds/removes a changedPath-derived term from seeds.seeds, and can add/remove an entry in filteredTerms (or change its documentCount/documentFrequencyRatio) EVEN WHEN the selected candidates[].{path,contentHash} set is byte-identical (same specs, same content, no genuine corpus/selection change). Because candidateSpecSetDigest hashes queryFiltering verbatim, this flips candidateChanged=true in persistInvalidationIfDrifted (review-inventory.ts:131-132), invalidating the OPEN epoch on a commit unrelated to the routing universe -- the same OPEN_REVIEW_INVENTORY_CANDIDATE_ROUTING_MUTATION false-positive class F-104 was filed to close, now recurring through the one field the fix left bound verbatim. The F-105 coverage in review-inventory-epoch-smoke.ts:735 only asserts a hand-constructed queryFiltering override moves reviewInventoryDigest (a digest-sensitivity self-check on the hash function itself, tautological w.r.t. hashing) -- it never calls buildKeywordSeeds/routeCandidateSpecs end-to-end to prove queryFiltering stays stable when candidates[].{path,contentHash} is unchanged but changedPaths churns, so this leak has zero regression coverage. Fix: (a) exclude queryFiltering (and any other seeds/changedPaths-derived diagnostic field) from candidateSpecSetDigest entirely -- it is diagnostic metadata about HOW candidates were selected, not WHAT was selected; keep only schemaVersion/mode/candidates-projected/scanEscalationReason, or (b) if queryFiltering must stay bound, strip changedPath-sourced seeds from the term set used to compute filteredTerms so it reflects only story-stable seed sources. Add an end-to-end regression test that holds candidates+corpus fixed, varies only changedPaths across two routeCandidateSpecs calls, and asserts candidateSpecSetDigest is unchanged.

findings.desc: Type-safety/crash-hardening gap, distinct from the already-resolved F-107/F-108 routing-semantics leak (do not conflate). review-inventory.ts:112 captureReviewInventoryScope does (validCandidate.candidates ?? findings.desc: WAVE 2/4 topology-critic verdict: saturation is NOT genuinely reached and the topology-critic receipt path remains mechanically blocked for BOTH verdicts (fourth independent live reproduction of F-089, now with additional AT_/PR_ diagnostics beyond F-089's original repro). Both `LATTICE_AGENT=lattice-review-topology-critic node ... topology_critic_receipt_set verdict=request_changes` and the read-only `topology_critic_receipt_check` fail identically with AT_TOPOLOGY_CRITIC_CONTEXT_INVALID / 'topology critic basis verification failed: AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING: PR_PLANNED_PATH_UNRESOLVED: planned path is unresolved: planned:B3F3D-005-H1:VPP-B3F3D-REPLAY-REPORT; basis semantic discovery digest mismatch; scope-contract digest mismatch; closure files hash mismatch; snapshot seal digest mismatch; freshness mismatch: evidence storyFilesHash does not match current story-owned file state'. This is a superset of F-089's original diagnostics (which listed only AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING/PR_PLANNED_PATH_UNRESOLVED/scope-contract digest mismatch); basis semantic discovery digest mismatch, closure files hash mismatch, and snapshot seal digest mismatch are new since F-089 was filed, meaning the acceptance-basis staleness has grown, not shrunk. Independently cross-confirmed by three additional mechanical evaluators run fresh this wave: `acceptance_topology_check --json` returns status=fail/structuralPass=false/result=inconclusive_basis_unverified with diagnostics AT_CLOSURE_FILES_STALE and AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING (identical message); `pre_review_check_read --json` returns status=inconclusive/ok=false with codes including PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED, PR_EVIDENCE_STALE, PR_CUTOFF_UNBOUND, PR_PLANNED_PATH_UNRESOLVED; `acceptance_rollout_check --json` returns mode=enforce/status=fail/ok=false/blocking=true/receipt=stale with diagnostics=[AR_REPORT_STALE], even though the underlying rollout report.verdict=pass and metrics.mislabeled3x1Count=0 (the receipt itself was a genuine, non-degraded full-envelope pass when generated -- it is only now stale, not fabricated). Direct hash comparison proves genuine drift, not a false positive: current git HEAD=2e7d83a08bc239261b649ba0aa7fe7a22e3601a7; review-inventory epoch RI-047 cutoff.headHash=70acae0bce247416ee072026512d47cf24bb8833; acceptance_rollout report.binding.headHash=a02963bd6e6ce6d02404cbd0d44f4820bb5bde52 -- three different hashes across three artifacts all claiming to bind 'current' state. SEPARATELY, independently re-verified the review-inventory epoch's own wave accounting is misleading (not a manufactured-saturation attempt, but a real rendering defect the operator must not rely on): the persisted epoch record (.lattice/story/actives/B-3f3d/review-inventory-epochs.json, epoch RI-047) has exactly ONE wave recorded, wave 1, with saturated=false and nextRunSequenceBoundary=454. `review_inventory_status` renders 'Current wave: 2/3' (correct: epoch.waves.length=1 plus 1 for OPEN state, meaning wave 2 is live/in-progress) but ALSO renders all five required lanes as 'pass', which is misleading: direct query of review-runs.json for ReviewRun sequence > 454 (the wave-2 candidate boundary) shows exactly ONE lane (lattice-review-quality, RR-455, backing RP-323) has any wave-2 evidence at all. lattice-review-concept, lattice-review-test-coverage, lattice-review-behavior, and lattice-review-docs have ZERO wave-2 ReviewRuns; their 'pass' rows are wave-1's stale terminals carried forward by the fallback `live?.lanes.find(...) ?? last?.lanes.find(...)` in renderReviewInventoryStatus (packages/main/src/handlers/review-inventory.ts:198), which silently backfills a genuinely-missing current-wave lane with the PRIOR wave's terminal in the human-readable status text. The gate itself is NOT fooled -- `live.missingLanes` correctly still includes those 4 lanes and the status correctly still reports Blockers: REVIEW_INVENTORY_LANES_INCOMPLETE with Next pointing at redispatching lattice-review-concept -- but the co-rendered lane rows create an internally self-contradictory status output (four lanes shown as pass while the blocker for those same lanes fires), which is exactly the kind of display an operator could misread as 'all lanes pass, saturation reached' when in fact 4 of 5 lanes have not run this wave at all. The one genuine wave-2 lane result (lattice-review-quality RP-323, RR-455) is itself real and substantive -- it correctly re-confirms F-111's gap is unfixed, correctly resolves F-112 as duplicate, and correctly re-verifies the F-096/F-097 check-position claim -- so this finding is not disputing that piece of work, only the claim that the wave as a whole, or the epoch overall, is saturated. CONCLUSION: saturation is not genuinely reached this wave (4/5 required lanes have zero current-wave evidence), and even if it were, this epoch/story cannot receive a signed topology-critic pass or request_changes receipt right now because the underlying acceptance basis is independently, mechanically, and currently confirmed stale across four separate evaluators. Recommended remediation, unchanged from F-089: regenerate acceptance_basis AFTER the scope-contract-changing commit, then rerun acceptance_topology_check/pre_review_check to confirm clean, before any topology-critic receipt is attempted again; separately, fix the renderReviewInventoryStatus lane-row fallback so a lane with zero current-wave candidate runs renders as 'missing' or 'pending', never as a carried-forward 'pass', to prevent this display artifact from being mistaken for genuine wave completion in future waves.
